items.text: Every staged scrum board file has valid frontmatter.
The shipped default and this project's checklist registry both pass the validator.
lib/skill-allow-list.json has no unstaged modifications, so a test run or postinstall has not silently rewritten the security-relevant allow-list.
No new file is added under docs/. That directory is only for content meant for the published site; maintainer-internal documentation belongs under project/documentation/.

I understand that skills, agents, hooks and scripts are created and edited in the root directories, and that .claude/ and .agents/ are generated outputs that are never the primary location for a change.
Deterministic, repeatable steps in this change are implemented as scripts rather than as inline instructions in a SKILL.md.
The working tree is clean, so what is released is exactly what is committed.
The project's test suite has been run and passes on the exact commit being released.
This release is being published from the public repository, not from this private one; this repository's role is to mirror to it.
If a new top-level directory or config file was added, .publicignore has been reviewed so nothing private is reachable through the paths the public mirror publishes.
